card.architecture: LTX-2 19B distilled i2v + per-frame PixelQuantize (ComfyUI-PixelHarness) — PIXEL-ART IMAGE-TO-VIDEO
card.summary: LTX-2 image-to-video with the deterministic pixel-art quantizer applied to every decoded frame. A locked palette keeps colours identical frame-to-frame (no pixel shimmer); the video model supplies motion, the quantizer supplies the pixel grid.
use_cases: pixel-art image-to-video (temporally consistent via a locked palette)
animating a pixel/sprite still without per-frame palette drift
card.pick_when: You want the animation output already pixel-quantized with a stable palette.

prompt.guidance: Describe the motion/scene in a sentence. The image is the first frame; the output is pixel-quantized.
prompt.example: she takes a step forward, arms swinging, a looping walk cycle
prompt.overview: For LTX-2 image-to-video, the prompt should briefly anchor to what the source image shows and then describe the motion, camera move, and any audio that unfolds from it.
prompt.instructions: LTX-2 (the 19B, Gemma-3 text-encoder model) wants one flowing cinematic paragraph with no line breaks, lists, or fragments, written entirely in present tense (walks, tilts, flickers). For image-to-video, briefly restate the subject and setting actually in the frame so the model stays consistent, then spend most of the prompt on what happens next: how subjects move, how the camera behaves, and how the scene goes from still to motion. State the camera's perspective, angle, movement, and speed explicitly, and include audio cues (dialogue in quotes, music, ambient sound) since LTX-2 generates synced audio. Keep it to roughly 3-6 sentences / under ~200 words.
do: Restate the image's actual subject and setting, then build motion on top of it
Write one flowing paragraph with no line breaks, bullets, or fragments
Use present tense for every action (walks, turns, drifts, flickers)
Name the camera perspective, angle, movement, and speed explicitly
Describe the transition from stillness into motion and how it resolves
Add audio cues - dialogue in quotation marks, music, ambient sound
Use concrete cinematographic and physical detail; keep it literal and ordered
dont: Don't redundantly over-describe static elements already visible in the image
Don't use line breaks, lists, headings, or keyword/tag spam
Don't write in past or future tense
Don't leave camera motion unspecified or contradict the source image
examples: A young woman stands at a rain-streaked cafe window holding a white ceramic mug, the warm interior lights glowing behind her. She slowly turns to face the camera and smiles as a soft breeze moves a loose strand of hair across her cheek, steam curling up from the mug. The camera begins as a static medium close-up, then gently pushes in at eye level over several seconds, the shallow depth of field softening the wet street outside. Quiet piano music plays beneath the faint patter of rain on the glass.

A red vintage convertible sits parked on a sunlit coastal road, its polished hood reflecting the bright sky. The car holds still as the camera tracks smoothly from left to right along its profile at hip height, reflections sliding across the chrome and paint while palm-frond shadows ripple over the surface. The move slows to a stop on the front grille as warm afternoon light flares across the windshield. Gentle ocean waves and distant gulls fill the background ambience.
prompt.negative_guidance: LTX-2 supports a negative prompt; the official default is 'pc game, console game, video game, cartoon, childish, ugly'. On the full (real-CFG) path - including the non-distilled 'dev' variant - negatives meaningfully shape the video (useful: subtitle, text, watermark, morphing, warping, flicker, jitter, shaky camera, deformed, extra limbs). On the distilled CFG~1 path they have little effect.

ui_help.note: LTX-2 video, pixelized per frame with a locked palette so the pixels don't crawl.
ui_help.good_for: pixel-art animation from a sprite still

edit_use_cases: pixel-art image-to-video: animate + quantize with a locked palette (LTX-2)
